newsitem.title: CANADA: Ranger shrs rise on takeover speculation.
newsitem.headline: Ranger shrs rise on takeover speculation.

text.p: Shares in Ranger Oil Ltd rose in busy trading on Friday as takeover speculation about the company again crept into the market, traders said.
Ranger shares were up 0.35 at 13.70, just below the 52-week high, on the Toronto Stock Exchange in heavy turnover of 2.26 million shares.
One trader said the rumored suitors being tossed around the market included Talisman Energy Inc and privately held Husky Oil.
Analyst Craig Langpap of Peters & Co said takeover speculation often circulates about Ranger.
"Every few months we start to see takeover speculation getting fed into Ranger's stock price," Langpap said.
He saw Husky and Talisman as unlikely bidders for the Calgary-based energy company.
"I would think there would be more speculation around PanCanadian (Petroleum Ltd )," Langpap said.
PanCanadian on Thursday unveiled plans to make an acquisition of international assets that could be valued at between C$1.0 billion and C$1.5 billion.

"We need 40 percent of that growth to come from the international side and we don't think we can get our international production up to 80,000 or 90,000 barrels a day without kickstarting it with some form of acquisition," PanCanadian chief executive David Tuer told reporters after the annual meeting in Calgary.
Ranger's international assets could supply a good portion of this desired offshore increase.
"Of course, these are all rumors," said the trader.
((Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com))
